problems.title: Problem 1: Complementary and Supplementary Angles
problems.prompt: Two angles $\angle A$ and $\angle B$ are supplementary. The measure of $\angle A$ is represented by $3x + 10^\circ$ and the measure of $\angle B$ is $2x + 25^\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the measure of each angle.
problems.problem: Two angles $\angle A$ and $\angle B$ are supplementary. The measure of $\angle A$ is represented by $3x + 10^\circ$ and the measure of $\angle B$ is $2x + 25^\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the measure of each angle.
problems.hint: Supplementary angles sum to $180^\circ$. Set up $(3x + 10) + (2x + 25) = 180$.
problems.solution: $5x + 35 = 180 \implies 5x = 145 \implies x = 29^\circ$. $\angle A = 3(29) + 10 = 97^\circ$. $\angle B = 2(29) + 25 = 83^\circ$. Check: $97^\circ + 83^\circ = 180^\circ$.

problems.title: Problem 2: Unique Triangle Conditions
problems.prompt: Can a triangle be constructed with side lengths $6\text{ cm}$, $9\text{ cm}$, and $16\text{ cm}$? Justify your answer using the Triangle Inequality Theorem.
problems.problem: Can a triangle be constructed with side lengths $6\text{ cm}$, $9\text{ cm}$, and $16\text{ cm}$? Justify your answer using the Triangle Inequality Theorem.
problems.hint: The sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be strictly greater than the third side.
problems.solution: No. The two shorter sides have a sum of $6 + 9 = 15\text{ cm}$, which is less than the longest side ($16\text{ cm}$). Because $15 < 16$, the sides cannot meet to form a closed triangle.

problems.title: Problem 3: Volume and Surface Area of a Right Triangular Prism
problems.prompt: A right triangular prism has a right triangle base with legs $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ (hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$). The height of the prism is $15\text{ cm}$. Calculate both the total volume and total surface area.
problems.problem: A right triangular prism has a right triangle base with legs $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ (hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$). The height of the prism is $15\text{ cm}$. Calculate both the total volume and total surface area.
problems.hint: Base Area $B = \frac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24\text{ cm}^2$. $V = B \cdot h$. $\text{Surface Area} = 2B + (\text{Perimeter of base} \cdot h)$.
problems.solution: $\text{Base Area} = \frac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Volume} = 24 \times 15 = 360\text{ cm}^3$. $\text{Base Perimeter} = 6 + 8 + 10 = 24\text{ cm}$. $\text{Lateral Area} = 24 \times 15 = 360\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Total Surface Area} = 2(24) + 360 = 408\text{ cm}^2$.

problems.prompt: A right triangular prism has a right triangle base with legs $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ (hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$). The height of the prism is $15\text{ cm}$. Calculate both the total volume and total surface area.
problems.problem: A right triangular prism has a right triangle base with legs $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ (hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$). The height of the prism is $15\text{ cm}$. Calculate both the total volume and total surface area.
problems.hint: Base Area $B = \frac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24\text{ cm}^2$. $V = B \cdot h$. $\text{Surface Area} = 2B + (\text{Perimeter of base} \cdot h)$.
problems.solution: $\text{Base Area} = \frac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Volume} = 24 \times 15 = 360\text{ cm}^3$. $\text{Base Perimeter} = 6 + 8 + 10 = 24\text{ cm}$. $\text{Lateral Area} = 24 \times 15 = 360\text{ cm}^2$. $\text{Total Surface Area} = 2(24) + 360 = 408\text{ cm}^2$.
